show_hn.story_text: I made an agent-native 3d/vfx engine. Agents are good at making interesting scenes in Blender/Unreal/Nuke/etc. But these tools are fundamentally limited compared to what coding agents are capable of. Many simplifying assumptions are baked into these tools in order to fit human authoring methods. In vork, agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. So, for example, almost every 3d engine assumes light moves in a straight line. Light near a black hole does not; so the best you can do in e.g. Blender is faking gravitational lensing. show_hn.story_text: I built the first version of this stuff a decade ago as ethanolus (c2h5oh). And I've used it for most of my projects as a backend layer since then. The main motive is to eliminate unnecessary complexity from backend layers. How it works: a rust nginx module calls postgresql functions via non-blocking libpq io. There is an optional patch for libpq. It provides zero-copy for nginx-chained memory buffers - to avoid request body copies between nginx and libpq. Pgxio supports http2 and websockets. Realtime listen/notify updates from postgres without polling. How to try - code on github. Tested on Debian - FreeBSD validation in progress. It's alpha - so any feedback is welcome.
